copy_pick.why: It avoids the 'Back home' and 'While…' shapes that recent cards keep reusing, carries the sports-desk voice through the roster headline, the 'ground games' opener and the 'full slate' sign-off, and names the orbital nuke story clearly, while Candidate 2 leans on the stale 'Meanwhile…Back home' struc

doom.driver: Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month. A nuclear detonation in space "could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites."
doom.blurb: RUSSIA SIGNS A NUKE TO THE ORBITAL ROSTER
doom.summary: Ground games are apparently too small now. Ukraine is sinking Russian corvettes off Libya, Russian drones keep straying into Poland, and Moscow's reported response is to put a nuclear warhead in orbit, where it could wipe out thousands of satellites at once. Meanwhile COP31 ended in a walkout, Trump personally rehired Nvidia's CEO over spy concerns, and Claude can now approve its own pull requests, so it was a full slate everywhere.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: GLM-5.4's loop transformer, Claude shipping its own code fixes, and METR's exponential curves all landed on the same day.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The White House brags it got Jensen Huang reinstated despite national security red flags, and Trump held at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: The war now reaches from Libya's ports to Polish airspace, while South Korea sends island residents to shelter as Russian jets approach.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: State attorneys general say Grok is still generating CSAM despite X's claims that every output is screened.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: An 80-pound delivery drone on a Detroit roof is the strangest entry on an otherwise quiet card.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. The camera sits on the wet asphalt of a German Autobahn service area at night and looks steeply upward. A huge blood-red and furnace-orange artificial aurora fills the sky, with rippling curtains of crimson and violet light and a few streaks of burning orange where dying satellites fall. The glow comes from a molten orange band along the horizon behind the buildings and washes the whole scene in hellish light. It paints the rain-slick tarmac, which reflects it in long orange streaks, and it lights the undersides of everything above. A tall overhead road gantry looms in the foreground. Its big electronic sign panels are blank grey-violet, with no navigation or traffic data. Beside it, a towering fuel-price pylon has a dead, unlit display. Behind it, the huge flat canopy of a powerless filling station is lit from below by the orange horizon glow, and its underside shows rows of dead tube lights. A stalled line of freight lorries fills the middle distance. Their amber hazard lights blink, and their cabs are lit orange. A lattice cell tower rises into the aurora with its antenna arrays hanging dead. A few small, whole truckers and travelers stand on the tarmac in bright orange rim light. They hold dead phones and paper road maps up toward the sky and look up at the red glow. The shadows are bruised violet and maroon. Everything on screen is clearly visible, and the mood is malevolent and wrong.

minor: The overhead gantry's right end stops in mid-air with no support, close to the separate price pylon.
The pink blob in the central traveler's hands, probably a map or phone, is hard to identify.
The faces of the travelers are tiny and faint, though they read fine as silhouettes looking up.
The fuel-price pylon's dead display is a column of dark boxes with red panels, which is slightly cluttered but has no readable text.
The trucks in the middle distance blend into each other in the orange glow.

dawn.driver: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali set for historic flight to China’s space station. The Pakistan Air Force pilot will spend about a week on board the Tiangong, conducting experiments with China’s crew.
dawn.blurb: A PAKISTANI PILOT RISES TO THE HEAVENLY PALACE
dawn.summary: Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot, is bound for China's Tiangong station, where he will spend about a week running experiments alongside the Chinese crew in a historic first for his country. Back on the ground, volunteers high in the Colombian Andes are planting the fuzzy frailejón one seedling at a time, protecting a plant that helps supply water to millions. And in Japan, researchers have built a gum disease treatment from egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light that clears out harmful bacteria while leaving the good ones in peace.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Japanese researchers unveiled a gum treatment that uses egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light to target harmful bacteria while preserving the mouth's healthy microbes.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Pakistan's Zeeshan Ali will join China's crew aboard Tiangong for a week of shared experiments, a historic partnership in orbit.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Bengals receiver Tee Higgins traded designer clothes for a Fiona the Hippo shirt, a sweet tribute that delighted all of Cincinnati.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: A growing band of volunteers in the Colombian Andes is replanting frailejones, the fuzzy water guardians that help supply water to millions.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Archaeologists found evidence that Verica, the Iron Age ruler who shaped Britain's history, may have been a woman, restoring a remarkable leader to the record.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 1 has the freshest structure, skipping the overused 'Elsewhere' pivot and the 'patient' echoes of recent cards, and its grand newsreel blurb slyly translates Tiangong as the 'Heavenly Palace' to name a real, historic first without any bad-news framing.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. INTERIOR SCENE inside a modest family living room in Islamabad on the clean, clear morning after Pakistan's first astronaut flew to China's Tiangong space station. We look from inside the room toward a wide open balcony doorway and window, which frame the outside world. Beyond them, soft green Margalla Hills rise over rooftops, water tanks and neem trees, under a pale apricot sky with a fading crescent moon. Warm amber morning light slants across a worn woven rug, and the last shadows are lifting from the corners. A low wooden table in the foreground holds a tray of empty chai cups and a plate with a few leftover sweets from the night-long watch. The dark TV is off, and cushions are pushed about where the family sat. Green-and-white paper bunting droops from the curtain rod, and a few crescent-and-star paper cutouts lie scattered on the floor. A cardboard model rocket and a child's crayon drawing of an astronaut with a green flag patch stand propped on the windowsill. Beside them sits a glass jar of vivid blue-green cyanobacteria, a school science project catching the sun. A grandfather in a cream shalwar kameez and white cap sweeps paper scraps toward the balcony door with a straw broom. A small girl in a school uniform stands whole at the window and gazes up at the empty sky. Calm, proud and hopeful mood, palette of warm amber, soft sage green and cream with gentle teal accents.

minor: The girl's legs and feet show in front of the low wall under the window, while her hands rest on the sill behind her. Her position relative to the wall is a little unclear.
The bottom-right corner has a striped, keyboard-like pattern where the sofa or rug edge should be, which is hard to read.
The scattered crescent cutouts on the rug are tiny and blend into the rug pattern.
The bunting flags are slightly uneven and some crescent shapes are muddy, but they read as bunting.
The objects on the windowsill (rocket model, bottle, drawing) are small and a bit crowded, but they are recognizable.
